_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Armenia covering Urartu, Orontid dynasty, Artaxiad empire (Tigranes the Great), Arsacid Armenia and first Christian state (AD 301), Bagratid kingdom, Armenian renaissance, Seljuk/Mongol invasions, Safavid-Ottoman partition, Armenian Genocide 1915, First Republic 1918, Soviet Armenia, Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, independence 1991, and 2020/2023 Artsakh losses.

religion.note: First nation to adopt Christianity as state religion (AD 301); Armenian Apostolic Church is autocephalous Oriental Orthodox

ethnic_groups.name: Armenian
ethnic_groups.notes: Indo-European; unique alphabet (Mesrop Mashtots, AD 405); diaspora ~7 million worldwide (more than homeland population); Genocide survivors' descendants

ethnic_groups.name: Yezidi (Kurdish)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest minority; Aragatsotn and Armavir regions; Yezidi religion; Kurdish-speaking; distinct from Muslim Kurds

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Assyrian, Greek, Ukrainian, Kurdish Muslim)
ethnic_groups.notes: Small Assyrian community; historically Greek community; post-2020 Artsakh Armenian refugees (~100,000) from Nagorno-Karabakh

current_leader.name: Nikol Pashinyan
current_leader.title: Prime Minister (head of government)
current_leader.notes: Civil Contract party; came to power via 2018 Velvet Revolution; lost 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war to Azerbaijan; Artsakh fell September 2023; peace negotiations with Baku ongoing

former_leaders.name: Levon Ter-Petrosyan
former_leaders.notes: First president; ANM; Karabakh war victor; resigned under pressure over Karabakh compromise proposal

former_leaders.name: Robert Kocharyan
former_leaders.notes: From Karabakh; hardliner; economic growth; March 2008 crackdown on protests

former_leaders.name: Serzh Sargsyan
former_leaders.notes: Republican Party; tried to continue as PM after constitutional change; ousted by Pashinyan's Velvet Revolution 2018

910.name: Urartu and Proto-Armenian Origins
910.description: The Kingdom of Urartu centered around Lake Van, its rivalry with Assyria, advanced metallurgy and irrigation, and the ethnogenesis of the Armenian people from Urartian and other Indo-European populations.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Urartu
sub_clusters.description: The rise of Urartu as a major Iron Age power in the Armenian Highlands, its monumental fortresses at Tushpa and Erebuni, and its eventual decline under Median and Scythian pressure.
key_events: Foundation of the fortress of Erebuni (Yerevan) by King Argishti I (782 BC)
Fall of Urartu to the Medes (c. 590 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Armenian Ethnogenesis
sub_clusters.description: The emergence of a distinct Armenian-speaking people from the merger of Urartian, Hurrian, and migrating Indo-European tribal groups in the Armenian Highlands.

910.name: Orontid Dynasty and Achaemenid Satrapy
910.description: Armenia under the Orontid dynasty as a satrapy of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, its participation in the Greco-Persian Wars, and the brief period of Seleucid overlordship.

sub_clusters.name: Achaemenid Armenia
sub_clusters.description: Armenian satrapies within the Persian Empire, their tribute obligations, military contributions to Persian campaigns including Xerxes' invasion of Greece, and the development of Armenian noble houses.

sub_clusters.name: Orontid Semi-Independence
sub_clusters.description: The Orontid dynasty's survival through Alexander's conquests, brief Seleucid suzerainty, and the transition to the Artaxiad dynasty following the Battle of Magnesia.

910.name: Artaxiad Dynasty and Tigranes the Great
910.description: The golden age of ancient Armenia under the Artaxiad dynasty, the vast empire of Tigranes the Great stretching from the Caspian to the Mediterranean, and the eventual Roman subjugation.

sub_clusters.name: Empire of Tigranes the Great
sub_clusters.description: Tigranes II's construction of the largest Armenian empire in history, founding of Tigranocerta, alliance with Mithridates VI of Pontus, and defeat by Roman general Pompey.
key_events: Tigranes crowned 'King of Kings' and builds Tigranocerta (c. 83 BC)
Defeat by Lucullus at Tigranocerta and submission to Pompey (69–66 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Roman-Armenian Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: Armenia as a contested buffer state between Rome and Parthia, the repeated imposition of client kings, and the erosion of Artaxiad sovereignty.

920.name: Arsacid Armenia and Christianization
920.description: The Arsacid dynasty of Armenia, the adoption of Christianity as a state religion in 301 AD — the first nation to do so — the invention of the Armenian alphabet, and the partition of Armenia between Rome and Persia.

sub_clusters.name: Adoption of Christianity
sub_clusters.description: King Tiridates III's conversion by Gregory the Illuminator, making Armenia the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion, and the establishment of the Armenian Apostolic Church.
key_events: Armenia adopts Christianity as state religion under Tiridates III (301 AD)
Gregory the Illuminator consecrated as first Catholicos of Armenia

sub_clusters.name: Invention of the Armenian Alphabet
sub_clusters.description: Mesrop Mashtots' creation of the Armenian alphabet in 405 AD, launching a golden age of Armenian literature, historiography, and theological writing.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of Avarayr and Partition
sub_clusters.description: The fall of the Arsacid dynasty, the partition of Armenia between Byzantine and Sassanid spheres, and Vardan Mamikonian's heroic stand at the Battle of Avarayr to defend Christianity.
key_events: Battle of Avarayr — Armenians fight Sassanid Persia to preserve Christianity (451 AD)

920.name: Medieval Armenian Kingdoms
920.description: The Bagratid Kingdom of Armenia, the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, and the cultural and commercial flourishing of the Armenian diaspora during the medieval period.

sub_clusters.name: Bagratid Kingdom of Ani
sub_clusters.description: The restoration of Armenian sovereignty under the Bagratuni dynasty, the magnificent capital of Ani as a 'city of 1001 churches,' and the Seljuk conquest.
key_events: Ani becomes capital of the Bagratid Kingdom and flourishes as a major city (961 AD)
Seljuk Turks conquer Ani after the Battle of Manzikert (1064 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia
sub_clusters.description: The Armenian kingdom established in Cilicia (southern Anatolia) by refugees from the Seljuk invasions, its alliance with Crusader states, and its final fall to the Mamluks.

sub_clusters.name: Arab and Seljuk Domination of Eastern Armenia
sub_clusters.description: Armenian principalities under Arab Caliphate rule, the Arminiya province, anti-Arab revolts, and the gradual reassertion of Armenian autonomy leading to the Bagratid restoration.

930.name: Mongol and Turkmen Rule
930.description: Armenia under successive waves of Mongol invasion, Timurid devastation, and the competing Turkmen tribal confederations of the Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu.

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Invasions and Ilkhanate
sub_clusters.description: The Mongol conquest of Armenia, the region's incorporation into the Ilkhanate, devastation of cities and population, and some Armenian-Mongol diplomatic cooperation against Mamluks.

sub_clusters.name: Timurid and Turkmen Period
sub_clusters.description: Tamerlane's devastating campaigns through Armenia, followed by Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen rule, and continued depopulation and destruction.

930.name: Ottoman-Safavid Partitioned Armenia
930.description: The partition of historic Armenia between the Ottoman and Safavid empires, the forced deportation of Armenians from the Ararat Valley by Shah Abbas I, and the flourishing of the Armenian merchant diaspora.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Western Armenia
sub_clusters.description: Armenian communities under Ottoman rule in the six vilayets, the millet system, and the social and economic life of Armenians in the Ottoman Empire.

sub_clusters.name: Safavid Eastern Armenia and Deportations
sub_clusters.description: Shah Abbas I's forced relocation of Armenians to New Julfa (Isfahan), creating a wealthy merchant colony, while eastern Armenia became a battleground between Safavid and Ottoman forces.
key_events: Shah Abbas I forcibly deports Armenians to New Julfa, Isfahan (1604–1605)
Armenian merchants of New Julfa build a global trade network spanning Asia and Europe

940.name: Russian Conquest and National Awakening
940.description: The Russian conquest of eastern Armenia from Persia, the Armenian cultural and national revival, the growth of revolutionary movements, and the escalating persecution of Armenians in the Ottoman Empire.

sub_clusters.name: Russian Annexation of Eastern Armenia
sub_clusters.description: The treaties of Gulistan and Turkmenchay ceding eastern Armenia from Qajar Persia to Russia, establishment of the Armenian Oblast, and the Russo-Turkish War outcomes expanding Russian-controlled Armenian territories.
key_events: Treaty of Turkmenchay — Eastern Armenia ceded from Persia to Russia (1828)
Russo-Turkish War gains Kars and Ardahan for Russia (1877–1878)

sub_clusters.name: Hamidian Massacres and Revolutionary Movements
sub_clusters.description: The rise of Armenian revolutionary parties (ARF, Hunchakian), the Hamidian massacres of 1894–1896 under Sultan Abdul Hamid II, and the Adana massacre of 1909.
key_events: Hamidian massacres kill an estimated 100,000–300,000 Armenians (1894–1896)
Adana massacre during the counter-revolution (1909)

950.name: Armenian Genocide and First Republic
950.description: The Armenian Genocide perpetrated by the Ottoman government during World War I, the Battle of Sardarabad, and the brief First Republic of Armenia.

sub_clusters.name: Armenian Genocide
sub_clusters.description: The systematic extermination of 1.5 million Armenians by the Ottoman government through deportations, death marches, and massacres — one of the first modern genocides.
key_events: April 24, 1915 — arrest and execution of Armenian intellectuals in Constantinople
Death marches and mass killings claim an estimated 1.5 million Armenian lives (1915–1918)

sub_clusters.name: First Republic of Armenia
sub_clusters.description: The declaration of the First Republic after the Battle of Sardarabad, the brief period of independence, the Turkish-Armenian War, and the forced Sovietization of Armenia.

950.name: Soviet Armenia
950.description: Armenia as a Soviet Socialist Republic: rapid industrialization and urbanization, the Stalinist purges, the Nagorno-Karabakh movement, the 1988 earthquake, and the drive for independence.

sub_clusters.name: Sovietization and Stalinist Era
sub_clusters.description: The Soviet takeover, the loss of Nakhchivan and Nagorno-Karabakh to Azerbaijan, forced collectivization, the Great Purge targeting Armenian intelligentsia, and industrialization.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Stalin and Cultural Revival
sub_clusters.description: The Khrushchev thaw, the 1965 mass demonstrations commemorating the Genocide, and a cultural and national revival within the constraints of Soviet rule.

sub_clusters.name: Karabakh Movement and 1988 Earthquake
sub_clusters.description: The mass movement for unification with Nagorno-Karabakh, the devastating Spitak earthquake killing 25,000, and the declaration of independence from the USSR.
key_events: Devastating Spitak earthquake kills approximately 25,000 people (1988)
Armenia declares independence from the Soviet Union (1991)

960.name: Independent Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh Conflict
960.description: Post-Soviet Armenia's struggle with the Nagorno-Karabakh wars, economic blockade, the 2018 Velvet Revolution, and the devastating 2020 and 2023 losses in Karabakh.

sub_clusters.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
sub_clusters.description: The full-scale war with Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, Armenian military victories, the capture of surrounding territories, and the 1994 ceasefire.
key_events: Armenian forces capture Shusha/Shushi and the Lachin corridor (1992)
Bishkek ceasefire agreement freezes the conflict (1994)

sub_clusters.name: Post-War Challenges and Velvet Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Economic hardship, political corruption, the October 27 1999 parliament attack, and the 2018 Velvet Revolution led by Nikol Pashinyan bringing democratic reform.

sub_clusters.name: Second Karabakh War and Aftermath
sub_clusters.description: Azerbaijan's 2020 military offensive recapturing surrounding territories, the 2023 offensive taking Nagorno-Karabakh entirely, the exodus of 100,000+ ethnic Armenians, and the geopolitical realignment.
key_events: 44-day war ends with Armenian defeat and Russian peacekeepers (2020)
Azerbaijan captures Nagorno-Karabakh; mass exodus of Armenian population (2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
